records: The usual amount of cinnamon, please.
Preserve the customary quantity, not a customary price or an invented number of units.
(...Someone's ahead of us.)
Hodram notices the earlier customer; keep this as an aside.
Coming right up. That'll be this much.
The trader quotes the displayed price without inventing a number.
Oh? Your price has gone up.
Carlo notices the higher quote before bargaining.
No, it hasn't. That's about what you always pay.
Keep the trader's denial as his own bargaining claim.
Ha ha! Don't be ridiculous, Adil. You think I don't know what you paid for it?
Use Adil only as the personal name supplied in this exchange; do not globally rename actor105.
Now, now...
The trader tries to deflect Carlo's challenge.
Considering this year's yield and the demand around here, I think you could do a little better.
Retain both supply and local demand as Carlo's basis for negotiation.
I could always try somewhere else. There's no law that says I have to buy from the same shop every time.
Carlo threatens to take his business elsewhere; no actual new law or exclusive contract is asserted.
Urgh... All right, all right. I can't get the better of you.
Keep the trader's reluctant concession without inventing the final discount.
Hm? Adil... Have you got a fever?
Carlo shifts abruptly from bargaining to concern for Adil's health.
What now, Carlo? Still finding fault with the way I do business?
Adil initially mistakes the health question for another bargaining tactic.
That's not it. You have a fever. Get to bed early tonight.
Preserve Carlo's concern and instruction within the fictional exchange; add no diagnosis beyond fever.
Oh, come on... Wait. I really am getting the chills.
Adil begins to recognize his symptoms; do not invent a named disease.
You see? I'll do my shopping tomorrow. Close up for today.
Carlo postpones his purchase so the trader can rest.
Hmm... I'll take your advice. Sorry, folks, but you'll have to come back tomorrow, too.
The closure also delays Hodram's party; preserve the apology and next-day timing.
Sorry about that. You came to do business, too, didn't you?
Carlo acknowledges the inconvenience to the waiting party.
How did you know he was ill?
Hodram asks how Carlo noticed the trader's condition.
He didn't have any color in his face.
Retain the visible complexion clue rather than inventing a medical examination.
Well, well. You're nearly as observant as I am.
Fernando's optional self-regarding compliment remains distinct from Carlo's explanation.
...(He didn't look ill to me.)
Hodram privately admits he missed the condition, setting up Carlo's unusual sensitivity.
Most people wouldn't notice. I'm rather sensitive to how people are feeling.
Carlo describes attention to others' health, without claiming a physician's credentials.
(Interesting...)
Keep Hodram's thoughtful aside.
Would you come to the trading post with me tomorrow morning? I think I can make up for today's inconvenience.
Preserve the place, morning timing and tentative offer to make amends.
Of course. I'll be there.
Hodram firmly agrees to the proposed meeting.
Carlo! Thank you for yesterday!
The innkeeper thanks him; no relationship to Adil is established by her label.
How's Adil?
Carlo immediately asks about the trader's condition.
Resting at home today, just to be safe.
Keep her report about Adil resting; do not turn home into their shared marital home.
Good. I hope he's better soon.
Carlo responds with straightforward concern.
He never listens to a word I say. Even yesterday, if you hadn't spoken up...
Preserve her frustration and unfinished thought without calling Adil her husband.
Oh, listen to me going on. You saved his life. I wanted to thank you properly.
The life-saving praise is her explicit assessment; no new treatment is invented.
Thank you. I appreciate it, but thank these travelers instead. They had to put off their business overnight.
Carlo redirects the reward to the inconvenienced party rather than taking it himself.
Oh dear, I'm sorry we held you up. It isn't much, but... Would you accept this?
Keep the offered gift unspecified in spoken prose; item mechanics must remain source-bound separately.
Thank you, ma'am. You're in a hurry, aren't you? Go ahead and do your shopping first.
Localize おかみさん politely without wife or mother; Carlo gives the travelers priority.
Carlo! Sorry about yesterday!
Adil unexpectedly appears after the report that he was resting.
You!
The innkeeper scolds him without an invented familial address.
Adil! You should be in bed!
Carlo also objects to the ill trader returning to work.
Hah! I'm fit as a fiddle. Can't spend a fine trading day like this lying in bed!
Preserve Adil's stubborn claim of good health and eagerness to trade; it is not a narrator diagnosis.
Honestly! There's no helping you!
Keep the innkeeper's exasperation without making her his spouse.
Ha ha! I'm glad you've got your energy back. But don't overdo it today.
Carlo is reassured by Adil's energy while still urging restraint.
I'll come by again tomorrow. Take care of these folks' business for me.
Carlo postpones his own transaction again and asks Adil to serve the travelers.
Take care of your family and your health. Well, goodbye.
Retain both explicit priorities as general advice, without inventing the travelers' family circumstances.
Hodram considers Carlo's words before stopping him.
...Wait a moment.
Hodram interrupts Carlo's departure to make an offer.
Hm?
Carlo turns back in response.
I was impressed by your bargaining yesterday. I'd like you aboard my ship.
Recruitment is prompted by Carlo's demonstrated commercial skill, not a newly invented sailing ability.
Now, where did that come from?
Keep Carlo's surprise at the abrupt offer.
I'm serious.
Hodram directly confirms the offer.
I'm no sailor. Just a merchant.
Carlo distinguishes his actual profession from seafaring work.
There's more to life aboard ship than sailing her. A purser has an important job to do, too.
Use the exact reviewed role term Purser for 主計長, not an improvised quartermaster or navigator station.
Carlo hesitates before Hodram asks about his reasons.
Don't want to leave here? Is it your children?
Hodram asks a mistaken question; children must not be treated as currently living.
I... don't have a family anymore. They died a year ago.
Preserve the explicit bereavement and one-year timing.
Keep Hodram's silence before Carlo's explanation.
My daughter fell ill first. There was an epidemic. I was so caught up in my work... I didn't look after her properly.
Carlo explicitly describes his daughter's illness and his own regret; do not diagnose a named disease.
Carlo (FE recollection)
By the time she got treatment, it was too late. My wife caught it, too... I lost them both.
Preserve delayed treatment, transmission to his wife and both deaths without inventing a treatment method.
Carlo (FE recollection)
I had no idea...
Hodram responds sympathetically to the disclosure.
After neglecting my family for it, my work felt empty. Ever since, I've cared more about everyone's health than about business.
Retain Carlo's self-blame and changed priorities without diminishing his continuing commercial skill.
So that's how you noticed he wasn't well...
Hodram connects the bereavement to Carlo's concern for Adil.
...What about going home?
The question opens a different possible destination rather than insisting he stay.
Venice? Too many happy memories there. I couldn't live there alone.
Preserve the paradox that happy family memories make returning alone unbearable; use the bound Venice label.
Allow Hodram's pause before offering companionship.
Carlo. Come with us. If you don't want to go back to Venice alone, that is.
Use his name for the familiar おやじ; no Father or Grandpa relationship is implied.
Carlo waits for Hodram to explain what the invitation offers.
Aboard ship, we all live and work as one. Think of us as your family.
The crew-as-family metaphor is explicit in the source and must not be weakened into mere employment.
You'd... be my new family?
Carlo explicitly recognizes the offered family metaphor; do not invent legal adoption.
That's right. And I wouldn't want to lose a man with your skills. ...Will you come?
Hodram combines personal warmth with respect for Carlo's ability.
...Thank you. I'd be glad to join you.
Carlo accepts gratefully after the emotional disclosure.
My name is Carlo Sinat. A pleasure to join you.
Retain the exact bound Carlo Sinat spelling; do not improvise Sinato from phonetic reconstruction.
